text:
The music is neither sweet nor good,
though well sung, my lady,
if it strays from the tune of the words;
instead it brings displeasure, vexation, and pain.

But if the music happens to sound
in keeping with what is sung,
instead of the grief it breeds in the soul,
it leaves her filled with sweet imaginings.

You, who can move mountains
to the sound of song, do not sing of anger,
nor of the secret sorrow that consumes me.

Let my tears remain mine alone;
sing instead of the beauty of your eyes:
the song will then accord with what is sung.

translation.title: To a Lady Who Asked Him for Something of His Own
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
